name: Aryan race
summary: The Aryan race is the nineteenth-century racial doctrine that a superior white 'Aryan' stock, in its fullest form the Germanic or Teutonic branch, created civilization by conquest and declines when its blood mixes with others. Gobineau gave it its scientific form, Chamberlain made it a creed of Teutonic destiny, and Nazi ideology adopted it as the 'master race' idea. Its own sources speak mainly to race, heredity, equality and racial mixing, and say little on economics, government or foreign policy.
scope: The Aryan race as a racial theory: Gobineau's Essay on the Inequality of Human Races (1853-55) and Chamberlain's Foundations of the Nineteenth Century (1899), as the Holocaust Encyclopedia and the Gale encyclopedias present them. It leaves out the Nazi regime's programmes and laws (National Socialism has its own entry), Nordicism, and the linguistic sense of Aryan (Indo-Iranian speakers).

notes: Themes searched: race and heredity, equality, mixing and marriage, democracy and government, religion (Christianity, Jews), immigration, economy. The two founding texts and two reference works hold nothing on economics, welfare, the environment, foreign policy or institutions beyond race and democracy; the Nazi regime's laws and programmes were not used because National Socialism has its own entry.
